surface: The column dropdown menu opened from the keyboard on a cell: its items one by one with the arrow keys, a checkable item, and Escape back to the grid.

steps.note: Shift+Alt+ArrowDown on the selected cell opens the menu of its column (Color) with the first item highlighted, which is what keeps Escape working for a screen reader. Required: the highlighted item's label and the menu role (NVDA says `menu item`, which holds the word). Finding: VoiceOver says nothing when the column menu opens: 9 of 9 opens on Chromium and 7 of 9 on WebKit over three runs, where the context menu in grid-core is announced. NVDA with Chromium names the menu as a table and says menu in some runs only, as it does for the context menu in grid-core.
ArrowDown moves the highlight to the next item.

The separator row between the two items is skipped by the keyboard, so the next announcement names an item, never a row of dashes. Unsure how a reader treats the skipped separator when it reads the menu in browse mode: this lane only drives the keys.

Read only is a checkable item (`menuitemcheckbox`, aria-checked false while no column is read only): its label and its state are each required. The role is not required here: NVDA names no role, and VoiceOver says `menu item`. VoiceOver reads `Read only menu item` with no state, on both browsers, and `Read only checked menu item` once the column is read only. It does the same on a well-formed ARIA menu: it says `checked` for a checked item and nothing for an unchecked one (its behavior).

Escape closes the menu and the focus should return to the grid. Opening the menu from the keyboard selects the whole column and clamps the focus cell to row 0 (filters-menu-focus-order.spec.ts), so the cell that holds the focus is Alice's Color, `Red`, not Bob's `Green` the scenario selected. Finding: NVDA and VoiceOver announce the document on every browser (the recording), as after the context menu: the focus leaves the grid.
The grid answers the next key: ArrowDown from the focus cell reads the cell below, Bob's `Green`. Silence or the document here means the focus never came back to the grid after the menu closed.
